narrationTexts: I'll start by getting the lay of the land.
The PR sheet stops at 2026-06-17 — let me check the commit log, which likely covers more.
I have what I need. Writing the 4.2.0 section now.
finalText:
Done — 4.2.0 section added to `CHANGELOG.md:3`.

## What I went through

380 commits and 127 merged PRs, both covering 2026-05-02 → 2026-06-17. The breakdown:

| Type | Count |
|---|---|
| chore (153, of which 105 are dep bumps) | 153 |
| refactor | 73 |
| test | 64 |
| ci | 33 |
| fix | 26 |
| docs | 20 |
| perf | 10 |
| feat | 1 |

So ~320 of 380 commits are invisible to anyone installing the package. The 12 changelog lines above are the real content.

## The judgment calls worth your attention

**Three things I put under Breaking that weren't labeled as breaking by anyone:**

- `fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403` (#4223) was filed as a fix. It is a fix, but it's a status-code change on an auth path — that breaks client error handling. This is the item most likely to generate support tickets.
- `refactor(api): drop the unused v1 export route` (#4152) — the author called it "unused." That's a claim about your telemetry, not something I can verify from the log. If "unused" meant "no internal callers," external callers may disagree. Worth a 60-second check before you ship.
- "stop re-exporting the internal error types" landed **eight separate times** across core, db, auth, billing, and jobs (2026-05-05 through 06-16). Individually each looks like tidying; collectively it's a removal of import surface. If those types were ever documented as importable, this breaks people.

**One thing I deliberately left out — please confirm:** the Node version. There are five `docs: note the minimum node version` commits, six `ci: run the suite on node 22`, and three `chore: pin the node version in .nvmrc`. That *looks* like a minimum-Node bump, which would be the loudest breaking change in the release. But "noting" a minimum isn't raising it, CI adding node 22 isn't dropping older versions, and none of the .nvmrc commits touch `package.json` at all (they modify `tsconfig.json`, `CODEOWNERS`, and `.editorconfig` — which is odd on its own). I couldn't confirm an actual `engines` change, so I didn't invent one. **Check whether `engines.node` moved; if it did, that's a Breaking entry and probably the headline.**

**The perf work has no home.** Ten perf commits — reusing parsed schemas between requests, skipping a JSON round-trip on hot paths, batching metric writes, dropping clones in mappers. Users would notice that, but your template says three headings, same order, so I didn't add a fourth. Say the word and I'll add a `### Performance` section, or fold the two or three most substantial ones into a line elsewhere.

**Two smaller omissions, on purpose:**
- Error-message wording was tightened in core, billing, and queue. I left it out because three of your test commits explicitly moved to "assert the error code, not the message" — that reads like a deliberate stance that messages aren't contract. Easy to add back if you disagree.
- All 16 dependency bumps are patch or minor at runtime (`fastify` 4.28.0→4.28.1, `pg` 8.12→8.13, `zod` 3.23.6→3.23.8, etc.). The only majors — `vitest` 1→2, `esbuild` 0.21→0.23 — are devDependencies, so they don't reach anyone installing you.

**One data-quality note:** the history has heavy duplication — `pino` is bumped 12 times to the identical version, and the PR sheet shows the same title merged by different authors on different dates (#4120 and #4121 are both "bump pino 9.2.0 → 9.3.1," merged the same day). The raw commit count overstates the work substantially. Doesn't change the notes, but don't read 380 commits as 380 changes.
